Who was the 17th century French trader who visited the mines of Andhra in search of fine gems and diamonds?
x:
Jean-Baptiste Tavernier, the famous French traveller and gem merchant, visited India several times during the 17th century. He travelled extensively through the Golconda Kingdom, including the famous diamond mines of Kollur on the banks of the Krishna River in present-day Andhra Pradesh. His travel accounts provide valuable information about the mining techniques, diamond trade and commercial prosperity of the Golconda region. Tavernier described the quality of Golconda diamonds, including the famous Koh-i-Noor and other legendary gems, making his writings an important historical source for the economic history of South India.
Hence, the correct answer is
Option (4).

s: Kohinoor Diamond was found in which mines?
x:
The world-famous Kohinoor Diamond was discovered in the Kollur Diamond Mines on the banks of the Krishna River in present-day Palnadu district (earlier Guntur district). During the Qutb Shahi period, the Kollur mines were among the richest diamond- producing centres in the world. Many famous diamonds, including the Kohinoor, are believed to have originated from these mines.
Hence, the correct answer is
Option (3).

s: Which of the following is not true about Gol Gumbaz?
o: It is the tomb of Muhammad Adil Shah.
There is no mosque and no arches near the tomb.
Its dome is one of the largest in the world.
x:
Gol Gumbaz, located at Bijapur (Vijayapura) in Karnataka, is the magnificent mausoleum of Muhammad Adil Shah, the seventh ruler of the Adil Shahi dynasty. It is famous for: • One of the world's largest masonry domes • The famous Whispering Gallery • Impressive arches and surrounding architectural structures
Therefore, the statement that there is no mosque and no arches near the tomb is incorrect.
Hence, the correct answer is
Option (2).
